title: Advertise only wired MCP tools
description: Objective: stop advertising 82 tools that always refuse. Measured at HEAD 1aa7cdc: generateStdioToolEntries loops ALL RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS (94) + RUNTIME_QUERY_KINDS (16) at packages/mcp/src/stdio/stdio-tool-schemas.ts:199-206, frozen as STDIO_TOOL_ENTRIES (:206); stdio serves it at stdio-server.ts:169/:213 and HTTP shares it verbatim at http/http-tool-bridge.ts:40/:202 ('There is no HTTP-only tool, by construction'). The daemon wires exactly 25 commands (Object.keys(PAYLOAD_KEYS), apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts:96-121) + 3 queries (work.get_context, graph.get, events.read - mcp-dispatch-port.ts:96/:104/:114). Deliverable: an OPTIONAL allowlist threaded into createStdioMcpServer and createHttpMcpAdapter (absent allowlist = current full advertisement, so @moe/mcp stays daemon-agnostic and existing consumers unchanged); apps/daemon passes its wired roster at both call sites (mcp-main.ts:37-44, mcp-http/mcp-http-host.ts:128-134). An allowlisted name not in the generated entries is a construction-time refusal with a stable code, not a silent drop. Update the two coverage-pinning tests (stdio-schemas.test.ts:52-58 'covers every command and query kind exactly once', stdio-server.test.ts:108-114 length pin) to cover both modes. NOTE: sibling task-c52d25a41d284f8c8482d3f128c451af (epic-bd387eeb) adds foundation.verification to the wired roster — derive the allowlist FROM the vocabulary, never hand-copy it, so that landing changes nothing here. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/mcp typecheck && test, pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && test (nonzero count lines), pnpm typecheck.
definitionOfDone: With the daemon's allowlist applied, ListTools on stdio AND HTTP returns exactly the wired roster (currently 25 commands + 3 queries, but asserted BY DERIVATION from PAYLOAD_KEYS and the served query kinds, never a hand-pinned number), and a mutation drill removing one wired kind from the vocabulary shrinks the advertised list.
Without an allowlist, advertisement is byte-identical to today's full set, asserted by the updated coverage tests.
An allowlist naming an unknown kind refuses at construction with a stable reason code, asserted exactly.
All four package gates exit 0 with nonzero Test Files count lines; pnpm typecheck exits 0; only explicit owned paths committed.
taskRails: The allowlist is an optional parameter; @moe/mcp must not import from apps/daemon (dependency direction is daemon -> mcp).
Derive the daemon's allowlist from daemon-command-vocabulary PAYLOAD_KEYS + the dispatch port's served query kinds; no hand-copied rosters.
Assert the reason code on the unknown-kind refusal; drill the derivation by removing a kind.

Assert list contents by NAME SET derived from the input kinds, never a hand-pinned count — task-c52d25a4 is growing the daemon roster in flight and a pinned number would redden on their landing.

Implement the seam: StdioServerOptions gains optional toolAllowlist; createStdioMcpServer (stdio-server.ts:207, LISTED_TOOLS at :169 becomes per-server filtered) and createHttpMcpAdapter (http-tool-bridge.ts: HTTP_LISTED_TOOLS at :40 is module-frozen today — it must become per-adapter filtered, with the module-level constant retained for the no-allowlist path so existing consumers see identical bytes) both honor it. Construction refusal for unknown kinds with the stable code from step 1. @moe/mcp must NOT import from apps/daemon — the option takes plain kind strings; dependency direction stays daemon -> mcp. Both files stay under 250 lines.

GREEN: `cd packages/mcp && pnpm exec vitest run --root ../.. packages/mcp/src` -> `Test Files  9 passed (9)`, `Tests  175 passed (175)`; `pnpm exec tsc --project tsconfig.json` clean.

Seam as planned, at SERVING not generation. `allowlistedToolEntries(allowlist)` lives beside the generator in stdio-tool-schemas.ts (both transports already import that module, so no new file and no new bridge): it refuses an unknown kind with MCP_TOOL_ALLOWLIST_UNKNOWN_KIND naming only the offender, refuses an empty list with MCP_TOOL_ALLOWLIST_EMPTY, collapses repeats (two entries sharing a tool name is a client-visible defect), and preserves the caller's order. `generateStdioToolEntries` and STDIO_TOOL_ENTRIES are untouched, so stdio-schemas.test.ts needed no edit.

stdio: `StdioServerOptions.toolAllowlist?: readonly string[]` (KINDS, not tool names — the caller never learns the dot-to-underscore rule). The module-level LISTED_TOOLS is now built through a `listedFrom` helper and RETAINED for the no-allowlist path, so an existing consumer gets the identical shared object; a server with an allowlist filters once at construction.

HTTP: `httpListedTools(allowlist)` in http-tool-bridge.ts returns the module-level HTTP_LISTED_TOOLS unchanged when absent, and `createHttpMcpServer` takes the resolved list with that same default. `createHttpMcpAdapter` resolves it EAGERLY, before the registry exists, which is what makes an unknown kind a construction failure rather than a first-request failure — the HTTP server object is only built when a session opens, so lazy validation would have refused at the wrong time. HTTP_LISTED_TOOLS stays exported with its shape unchanged (planning risk 2).

No import from apps/daemon anywhere in @moe/mcp: the option is plain kind strings. Dependency direction unchanged.

LINE-CAP DISCLOSURE: stdio-server.ts 245, stdio-tool-schemas.ts 245, http-tool-bridge.ts 240 — all under the 250 target. http-server.ts is 327, but it was ALREADY 317 before this task and my change is +10 (the option field, the eager resolve, the extra parameter). - C: real derivation restored, kind still removed -> `Tests  7 passed (7)` and the roster measured 28. The advertised list SHRANK with the vocabulary, which is DoD 1's drill clause.
- D: vocabulary restored, roster back to 29. Both files sha256-verified byte-identical, and the restore of the peer-owned vocabulary was GUARDED: it only wrote back after confirming the file still held my mutation, so a peer write during the window would have aborted the restore instead of clobbering them.

reviewSummary:
Approved on evidence. Commit c382453, 13 files by pathspec.

Measured the honest-surface effect myself with a throwaway probe driving the production derivation: wiredMcpToolKinds() -> 29 kinds, allowlistedToolEntries() -> 29 advertised tools, against 110 generated. 26 wired commands + 3 served queries; the number appears nowhere in the code.

DoD 1 drill clause, done my way: deleting "session.renew" from PAYLOAD_KEYS moves the advertised roster 29 -> 28 (re-measured under mutation, vocabulary restored byte-identical, git status clean). The advertisement is derived, not copied.

DoD 3: replacing the unknown-kind throw in allowlistedToolEntries with `continue` reddens both construction cases by name — stdio "refuses an unknown kind AT CONSTRUCTION with its stable code" and http-parity "refuses an unknown allowlisted kind at adapter construction, with the stable code".

DoD 2: making the no-allowlist path return a truncated list reddens "advertises the full generated set on both transports without an allowlist" and nothing else, so byte-identity is pinned, not assumed.

Gates re-run by me: @moe/mcp typecheck 0; @moe/mcp test 0, 9 files / 175 tests; @moe/daemon typecheck 0; @moe/daemon test 0, 152 files / 3291 tests. The daemon red recorded at gate time has cleared — it was the registryKinds roster during task-c52d25a4's landing window.

Three disclosures I verified rather than took on faith, none a DoD gap:
- callTool still resolves through the unfiltered STDIO_TOOL_INDEX (stdio-server.ts:159, http-tool-bridge.ts:187): an advertisement filter, not an authorization boundary; a non-advertised name still reaches the daemon and is refused there. DoD 1 and epic rail 3 both speak about the advertised list.
- http-server.ts is 327 lines, over the 250 target, under the 400 cap; it was 317 before this task.
- Repo-wide pnpm typecheck is exit 1 now from an UNTRACKED peer file (control-room live-board-readonly.test.tsx), postdating the 20:21 green.
